headline: ‘We got guys who want to be here’: Blue Jackets’ Fantilli looks back on Marchenko trade
take:
Daily Faceoff reports that Blue Jackets center Adam Fantilli looked back on the Marchenko trade, with Marchenko's request granted ahead of the 2026-27 season and the winger dealt to the Toronto Maple Leafs. Fantilli said Columbus has "guys who want to be here."

The numbers say both teams have work to do. So far this season, CBJ (3-4-0) has controlled 44.2% of expected goals, which measures the quality of chances each side creates, and has scored 2.8 fewer goals than those chances would predict. Its goalies have saved 2 more goals than expected, so the Blue Jackets' problems are in creating offense, not stopping it. TOR (4-4-2) sits at 46.8% of expected goals and is about even with its chances, scoring 0.6 fewer than expected. The Leafs get more from their goaltending, with 5 goals saved above expected. At 5-on-5, though, TOR is at 44%, which is weaker than CBJ's 48%. For Marchenko, the move lands him on a team that is leaning on its goalies and its power play (0.79 expected goals per game, against 0.57 for CBJ). That makes the man advantage the most likely place for him to matter.
